body:
I met up with my friend after we both got out of work.  We had both had a pretty stressful day, so we decided to get really stoned.  We both got in his car and decided that the best place to roll the blunt would be the local supermarket's parking lot.  After rolling the blunt, we drove around on the back roads just smoking, talking about how our days were, and of course, discussing women.
[Erowid Note: 
Driving while intoxicated, tripping, or extremely sleep deprived is dangerous and irresponsible because it endangers other people.
Don't do it!
]
No later than when I had exhaled my last hit (about my 12th) is when I got that really goofy part of the high.  Everything that Tyler (the friend) said was just unbelievably funny.  In fact, I remember feeling like my heart was going to explode if I were to laugh any harder.  This went on for about 20 minutes.  Then all of a sudden I looked at the stars (it was pretty clear outside considering that it had rained a few hours ago), and I was entranced by them.  I remember thinking how small stars look in the sky, but in actuality how massive they really are.  I kept thinking about space, and time, about how many stars are still undiscovered due to the fact that they are still light years away.
I then started thinking about the possibility that there may be another life form out there, but that we could be the greatest life form in existance.  I was so deep into my own thought pattern that I didn't see Tyler put in his Moby cd.  So for the next 5-10 minutes we both sat in silence listening to Moby.  Then by pure coincidence, we just happend to look at each other, he saw my eyes, and I saw his, and we both lost it.  We were laughing so hard that we had to pull the car off to the side of the road to compose ourselves.  After about another hour we decided to head our seperate ways.  After I was home I laid in bed for about 45 minutes just thinking about how we seemed to look at each other at the right moment.  I looked at my clock and couldn't believe it said 3:30.  This whole experience taught me one thing:  You might as well kill time, because in the end time will kill you.
